headline: Govt unveils 5 relief measures for HSC examinees amid protests
summary: Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin announced steps to address weather disruptions and flawed exam questions to calm protesting students.
details: HSC examinees have been protesting in Dhaka and Savar over heavy rain, waterlogging, and errors in the Physics First Paper exam, as well as controversial remarks by the Education Minister.

Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin announced five relief measures to address weather-related disruptions. Local administrations can now change centers, postpone tests, or extend exam time based on conditions.
Students who missed exams due to adverse weather will be allowed to retake them with Chattogram board candidates using the same question papers on dates set by the ministry.

Regarding the flawed Physics First Paper, the government has decided to award full marks for the two erroneous questions. Those responsible for preparing the questions have been temporarily suspended.
Mahdi Amin defended the decision to continue the exams, stating that tests were held peacefully at 2,583 centers across the country after consultations with various stakeholders.
Meanwhile, a group of protesting students has suspended their protests and submitted a 6-point charter of demands to the Secretariat, dropping their call for the Education Minister's resignation.
caption:
Full marks for flawed questions and flexible exam centers: the government responds to HSC protests.

HSC examinees have been protesting in Dhaka and Savar over heavy rain, waterlogging, and errors in the Physics First Paper exam, as well as controversial remarks by the Education Minister.

Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin announced five relief measures to address weather-related disruptions. Local administrations can now change centers, postpone tests, or extend exam time based on conditions.

Students who missed exams due to adverse weather will be allowed to retake them with Chattogram board candidates using the same question papers on dates set by the ministry.

Regarding the flawed Physics First Paper, the government has decided to award full marks for the two erroneous questions. Those responsible for preparing the questions have been temporarily suspended.

Mahdi Amin defended the decision to continue the exams, stating that tests were held peacefully at 2,583 centers across the country after consultations with various stakeholders.

Meanwhile, a group of protesting students has suspended their protests and submitted a 6-point charter of demands to the Secretariat, dropping their call for the Education Minister's resignation.

headline: World Cup: Argentina and England clash in high-stakes semifinal
summary: After a one-sided France-Spain match, football fans look to Messi's Argentina and Tuchel's England to deliver a classic heavyweight encounter.
details: Lionel Messi's Argentina and Harry Kane's England face off in the second FIFA World Cup 2026 semifinal. The match takes place Thursday at 1:00 am Bangladesh time.
The world's top four teams had reached this stage, but the first semifinal between Spain and France saw Spain dominate completely, leaving many neutral fans disappointed by the lack ofs spectacle.
Argentina enters the match with 39-year-old Lionel Messi leading the charge. He has scored eight goals to help his side secure hard-fought knockout wins over Cape Verde and Egypt.

England, managed by Thomas Tuchel, has reached the semifinal through a steady but less dazzling performance. Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored 12 of England's 13 total goals in the tournament.
The rivalry between the two nations is legendary, marked by historic moments like Maradona's 'Hand of God' and the 1998 red card of David Beckham, as well as long-standing political tensions.
While both managers, Lionel Scaloni and Thomas Tuchel, have downplayed the political weight of the match, the encounter is expected to be more evenly balanced than the first semifinal.
The winner will face Spain in the final on Monday, as the European champions have set the benchmark for the tournament so far.
caption:
Can Messi and Kane deliver the classic semifinal the world has been waiting for?

Lionel Messi's Argentina and Harry Kane's England face off in the second FIFA World Cup 2026 semifinal. The match takes place Thursday at 1:00 am Bangladesh time.

The world's top four teams had reached this stage, but the first semifinal between Spain and France saw Spain dominate completely, leaving many neutral fans disappointed by the lack ofs spectacle.

Argentina enters the match with 39-year-old Lionel Messi leading the charge. He has scored eight goals to help his side secure hard-fought knockout wins over Cape Verde and Egypt.

England, managed by Thomas Tuchel, has reached the semifinal through a steady but less dazzling performance. Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored 12 of England's 13 total goals in the tournament.

The rivalry between the two nations is legendary, marked by historic moments like Maradona's 'Hand of God' and the 1998 red card of David Beckham, as well as long-standing political tensions.

While both managers, Lionel Scaloni and Thomas Tuchel, have downplayed the political weight of the match, the encounter is expected to be more evenly balanced than the first semifinal.

The winner will face Spain in the final on Monday, as the European champions have set the benchmark for the tournament so far.
